title: fix(react): republish an equal object definition as the same object (objectui#10106)
body:
Fixes #10106

Clause-②: no — a provider's republish identity. No exported symbol and no key on a published payload moves. Re-declared from the actual diff: the diff adds a module-private `isEqualPayload` and a `settle` closure inside `useSettledSchema`'s effect; the hook's exported signature, its `SettledSchema` interface and every key on the value it publishes are byte-unchanged.

## The re-take — it REPRODUCES

The card was wholly second-hand (filed from objectui#10036's hand-back, re-run by nobody), so the first deliverable was the measurement, not a diff. Taken first-hand on the REAL consumer, `ObjectGantt`, with an instrumented adapter, swapping the adapter on provider `object`, three cases in ONE command so that "two" is a discrimination and not a counting artefact of the harness:

| swap | `find` on the new adapter | expand sets |
|---|---|---|
| byte-identical answer, as a FRESH object (SUBJECT) | **2** | `[['owner'], ['owner']]` |
| the SAME def object from both adapters (CONTROL) | **1** | `[['owner']]` |
| a genuinely DIFFERENT def (CONTROL) | **2** | `[['owner'], ['owner','account']]` |

The middle row is what makes the top row a finding: the same harness counts ONE the moment the producer keeps the payload's identity, so the extra query is the republish and nothing else. The bottom row is where two queries are WARRANTED — the second carries an expand set the first could not have — which is why the repair may never be "fetch less".

After the repair, re-measured in the same harness: SUBJECT **2 → 1** (`[['owner']]`), and both controls unchanged (**1** and **2**, the latter still widening to `['owner','account']`).

`getObjectSchema` was called exactly once on the new adapter in every case, before and after: this is not "the refetch was skipped".

## What was repaired, and where

`AGENTS.md` §5 commandment #10 closes with two halves:

> a provider that refetches may not republish an equal payload as a new object, and a consumer that needs stability keys on the data, not on a cache

The consumers are already on the right side of the second half — `ObjectGantt`, `ObjectCalendar`, `ObjectView`, `ObjectTimeline` and `ObjectGallery` each key their record fetch on `def`, the payload, not on a memo identity. The breach was the first half, at the producer: `useSettledSchema` re-read `getObjectSchema` on an adapter change and settled a fresh `def` object for a byte-identical answer, re-firing every one of those fetches.

The fix is at that producer and nowhere else: a settle whose answer is value-equal to the one already published keeps the object consumers hold. Nothing moved into a consumer's dependency list, and no cache was introduced — commandment #10 names both as the wrong cure in the same sentence.

Why `ready` does not save anyone here, since it is easy to misread: `ready` is `resolution.key === key`, and an adapter swap does not move the key. `ready` stays TRUE right through the swap, so a consumer's gate holds nothing back — the first query goes out at once on the definition already in hand, and the republish adds the second. That is now pinned too.

## Evidence

**RED-before** — the pin run against the hook byte-identical to `origin/main`, with the file state proved in the SAME command (`git hash-object` on the hook equal to its `HEAD` blob, both printed as `bb550f98d`): `2 failed | 3 passed`. The two subject assertions failed; all three controls passed.

**GREEN-after** — same pin with the repair on disk (blob `f287de8b6`, printed in the same command): `5 passed`.

**Ablation from the committed state** — the `settle` bail-out replaced by the pre-repair unconditional republish. The mutation was proved by content and by hash, never by an exit code: injected marker count `1`, removed-guard count `0`, blob `f287de8b6 → ae320ff3b`. The pin went `2 failed | 3 passed` — the same two, with all three controls still green. Restore proved the same way: blob back to `f287de8b6`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

**Suites** — `packages/react` in full plus every `useSettledSchema` consumer pin (`ObjectGantt` fetch gate, `ObjectCalendar`, `ObjectKanban` x2, `ObjectGallery`, `ObjectTimeline`, `ObjectTree`, `ObjectView`) and the two doc-example reader gate suites: **115 files / 1353 tests passed**, at `fe23217e9` with a clean tree (printed in the same command).

**Type-check** — `@object-ui/react`: `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, both clean. The test project SELECTS the new pin (`--listFiles` finds it).

**Gates, re-run last, at `fe23217e9` with nothing unstaged** — `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:doc-examples`, `check:doc-example-ids`, `check:doc-example-readers`, `check:doc-snippets`, `check:doc-types`, `check:readme-exports`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major`, and `eslint` on both changed files: all exit 0.

⚠️ `check:doc-examples` and `check:readme-exports` first answered PRECONDITION NOT MET / population COLLAPSED (no `dist` on disk — `readme-exports` reported `typesResolved: 0` against a floor of 2). Those runs are recorded as not-a-verdict, not as passes. Both were then re-run properly after `turbo run build` over the filter the gate itself prints, and the green above is from those runs, with a healthy population (`readme-exports`: 3384 export symbols from 36 of 40 packages, 58 keys compared).

**Changeset** — decided by running the gate, not from memory: `check-changeset-presence` exited 1 and named `@object-ui/react`; a `patch` changeset was added and it now exits 0.

## Acceptance notes

Noted while in the file, ⛔ not filed and ⛔ not fixed here:

- `useSettledSchema.test.ts`'s case "re-fetches when dataSource identity changes even if the key does not" carries a comment stating "Ready flips false the instant the source changes, same mechanism as a key change". That is not what the code does: `ready` is `resolution.key === key` and an adapter swap leaves the key alone, so `ready` stays true — which is exactly the mechanism this card rests on. The assertions in that case are correct and still pass; only the sentence is wrong. Left alone because it is a different class from this card's defect, and correcting someone else's prose is not this card's business; the correct statement is now written and pinned in the new file next to it.

## Not in scope, deliberately

- The count is pinned at the hook's own boundary, through the consumer recipe the hook's `@example` publishes, because this card's file surface is `useSettledSchema.ts` and its tests. The `ObjectGantt` reading above was taken with a throwaway probe, reported here and removed — it is not part of the diff.
- PR #10100 (objectui#10036) neither caused nor fixes this; it is still open and touches `packages/plugin-gantt` only, so there is no overlap with this branch.
